Approximately 3,000 URS employees were furloughed during parts of the October 2013 U.S. federal government shutdown, and a number of employees working on DOD projects experienced work-week reductions; URS linked reduced federal spending to canceled and delayed projects.

While the full Amazon Board has overall responsibility for risk oversight, the Board has delegated responsibility related to certain risks to the Audit Committee and the Leadership Development and Compensation Committee.
Whole Foods Market states that its salary and benefits programs reflect its philosophy of egalitarianism.

Whole Foods Market operates three seafood processing and distribution facilities, a specialty coffee and tea procurement and roasting operation, and 11 regional distribution centers focused primarily on perishables distribution.

Clark, Ph.D., who previously served as Senior Vice President of Global Public Policy and External Affairs and Chief Sustainability Officer of Kellogg Company and who then served on the boards of Mead Johnson Nutrition Company and AdvancePierre Foods.

Dr. Thomas Middelhoff was a Director of America Online (since May 1995) and Chairman of Bertelsmann AG; he was nominated pursuant to a Common Stock Purchase Agreement with Bertelsmann AG, and the proxy stated Bertelsmann AG was a joint venture partner and that Dr. Middelhoff disclaimed beneficial ownership of 14,414,240 shares owned by Bertelsmann AG.

America Online's 1992 Employee, Director and Consultant Stock Option Plan provided that upon specified change-in-control events, outstanding unvested options would become fully vested upon the earliest of the normal vesting date, one year from the change in control, or an involuntary employment action.

Time Warner reported that in August 1999 TWE received a MediaOne notice terminating MediaOne's covenant not to compete; as a result of that notice and the TWE partnership agreement, MediaOne's governance and management rights over TWE terminated immediately and irrevocably to the fullest extent permitted by Section 5.5(f), including loss of Cable Management Committee participation and loss of TWE Board of Representatives votes on TWE businesses, while MediaOne retained certain protective governance rights on limited matters affecting TWE as a whole.

Bankers Trust reported results principally through eight broad Organizational Units: five product/service units (Investment Banking; Risk Management Services; Trading & Sales; Private Client Services Group; Global Institutional Services) and three geographic units (Australia/New Zealand; Asia; Latin America) delivering the same types of products with local expertise.

The 1997 annual report described a Group Executive Committee planned from 1 April 1998 that would include, besides members of the Board of Managing Directors, members of the Divisional Boards, heads of Staff Divisions, and Regional Chief Executive Officers.
Only nonemployee directors served on Exxon's Audit, Board Compensation, and Board Affairs committees.

In the first nine months of 1998 Exxon acquired a total of 37.5 million shares of common stock for the treasury at a cost of $2,537 million under its ongoing repurchase program (increased repurchases announced in the first quarter of 1997 plus benefit-plan offset purchases).
Exxon's Board reviews development and succession plans for Exxon's top executives.
Exxon's Board Compensation Committee set the salaries for Exxon's other elected officers.

Mobil's Board recommended against the CREF proposal on the grounds that it would deprive the Board of a means to protect stockholders' interests by deterring or repulsing coercive, two-tier and bargain-price offers, and that it could curtail the Corporation's ability to issue preferred stock for financings, acquisitions and additional equity capital.
To improve profitability in Japan, Mobil implemented initiatives to enhance revenue and reduce expenses, including the elimination of approximately 300 positions by year-end 1998.

Yanpet II, a $2.5 billion expansion of the Yanpet petrochemical complex in Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, which Mobil owned jointly with Saudi Basic Industries Corporation and which was to be completed in 2000, would more than double the complex's capacity and increase by almost 50 percent Mobil's worldwide capacity to make olefins derivatives.

At least annually, the Audit Committee reviewed the services performed and the fees charged by the independent auditors and determined that the non-audit services rendered did not compromise their independence.
Mobil nonemployee directors could not participate in Mobil's incentive compensation or other employee benefit programs.

Mobil's Board had defined events that might precede a major challenge to control: (1) a date is set for a stockholders' meeting to consider a business combination; (2) an interested stockholder begins to solicit proxies to propose election or removal of a director or a business combination; (3) announcement of a serious tender offer; or (4) any stockholder or group of stockholders acting in concert owns beneficially or has acquired the right to vote shares representing more than 25 percent of Mobil's outstanding stock.
